points: This chapter focuses on one sin: lashon hara. Rabbi Motzen says we often treat it as a sin everyone stumbles in, but we really can do better.
Yirmiyahu would rather live alone than in a society like this. Their tongue is like an arrow: a negative word keeps flying and doing damage far away.
No one trusts anyone. People say one thing to your face and another behind your back, and the whole fabric of society falls apart.
The punishment here is the land becoming empty. It's really a consequence: a society that always speaks badly of each other can't hold together.
"Al yishallel chacham b'chochmaso": wisdom, strength and wealth are gifts from Hashem. We can only be proud of how we choose to use them for good.
